content.title: About
content.content: Tahini is a paste made from ground toasted sesame seeds, widely used in Middle Eastern, Mediterranean and Asian cuisines. It has a creamy texture, nutty aroma and a slightly bitter taste. Tahini serves as the base for hummus, baba ganoush, sauces, desserts and baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tahini is made from fully toasted sesame seeds, which gives it its distinctive flavor.
In Israel, tahini is considered a national staple and appears in almost every dish.
Sesame is one of the oldest cultivated plants, grown for more than 5,000 years.
Tahini is often used in vegan recipes as an egg or dairy substitute.
In some countries tahini is sold as a runny paste, while in others it is thick, almost chocolate‑like.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Tahini contains monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Sesame is one of the richest plant sources of calcium, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Tahini helps replenish iron stores, especially important in vegetarian diets.

items.title: High in magnesium
items.content: Magnesium in tahini supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Sesamol and sesamin are antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Sesame allergy
items.content: Sesame is a major allergen; reactions can be severe.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Tahini is calorie‑dense, so portion sizes should be moderated.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Sesame contains oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use tahini as the base for sauces (hummus, tahini sauce), blend into smoothies, desserts, baked goods, salad dressings and marinades. It can be thinned with water, lemon juice and spices to create a smooth sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store tahini in a tightly sealed jar in a cool, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator, where it stays fresh for up to 6 months. Discard if it develops a rancid smell or taste.
